entities.name: Petro Doroshenko
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Petro Dorofiiovych Doroshenko was a Cossack political and military leader, Hetman of right-bank Ukraine (1665–1672) and a Russian voivode.

He played a crucial role in the Cossack–Polish War, leading the Cossack forces to several victories against the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. Doroshenko's military campaigns resulted in the signing of the Treaty of Bakhchysarai, which established the Hetmanate of Ukraine as a semi-autonomous state within the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.

Doroshenko's legacy extends beyond his military achievements. He was a key figure in the development of the Ukrainian Cossack identity and played a significant role in shaping the country's political and social landscape in the 17th century.

Despite his importance, Doroshenko's life was marked by controversy and power struggles. His relations with the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth were tense, and he was eventually forced to flee Ukraine after the Treaty of Andrusovo in 1686.

Today, Doroshenko is remembered as a national hero in Ukraine, and his legacy continues to inspire Ukrainian patriotism and identity.
